visual_cadence.notes: Measured over the creator's content, 0 to 161.2 s. A 'new composition' is a peak in structural change, where more than half of the ink mask changes within 0.4 s, with peaks merged inside 0.6 s. There are 84 of them in 161 s: median 1.30 s between them, mean 1.89 s, p10 0.77 s, p90 3.72 s. The rate changes through the video. In the hook (0 to 10 s) a new composition arrives about every 1.1 s (1.5, 2.43, 3.47, 4.63, 5.8, 6.47, 8.13, 9.13 s). Later the average is about 2.0 s, with some explanatory holds of 4 to 6 s (for example 15.8 to 20.2 s and 22.9 to 28.6 s). There are also smaller animation events that do not replace the composition: an element pops in, slides, tilts or drops. Counting every motion onset that follows a still hold gives 107 onsets, with a median of 1.03 s between them. One motion burst (from movement start until the pixels settle) lasts a median 0.37 s (p25 0.17, p75 0.50, p90 0.70). Speech density: the reference voice is fast, about 5 words/s (272 caption groups × 2.92 words in about 160 s). V01 runs at 2.55 words/s (147 words in 57.68 s), so the reference gives about 1 new composition per 9.5 words and 1 motion event per 7.5 words.

visual_layout.notes: Measured at 2 fps on the ink bounding box above the caption band. The composition is centred horizontally (bbox centre x is 289 of 576, so 50%). Bbox centre y has a median of 428/1024 = 41.8%, with p10 41.1% and p90 45.2%. At 1080x1920 that is a centre near y = 800 px. Width: median 68% of the frame width (about 735 px at 1080), p90 81% (about 875 px), p10 33%. Height: median 18% of the frame height (about 345 px), p90 32% (about 620 px). The visual band runs from about 25.6% (p10 of the top edge, about 491 px) to 59.4% (p90 of the bottom edge, about 1140 px), which leaves about 160 px of empty space above the caption. Within a composition, elements sit on a symmetric centre line: horizontal rows of circles, centred pyramids, or a pair of objects mirrored about x = 50%. Typical primitive sizes at 576 wide: small circles 25 to 30 px, the red 'protagonist' circle 60 to 80 px, large hero shapes 130 to 210 px. Elements may cross the caption band briefly; at 80.7 s a circle passes over the caption and is drawn on top of it. At 1080 a width above about 800 px enters TikTok's right 140 px zone, so cap the width there.

entrances.type: scale-up pop from 0 (small primitives: dots, circles)
entrances.notes: Measured at 120.13 s, two dots popping into grid cells at the same time. Diameter per frame at 30 fps: 0, 19, 31, 42, 48, 53, 56, 57, 58, 58 px. Normalised this is 0.33, 0.53, 0.72, 0.83, 0.91, 0.97, 0.98, 1.0. A 9-frame cubic ease-out gives 0.30, 0.54, 0.70, 0.83, 0.91, 0.96, 0.99, 1.0. The size never exceeds the final value, so there is no back or elastic easing. The pop starts in the same frame that the karaoke highlight reaches the triggering word.

entrances.type: grow / rescale of an element already on screen
entrances.notes: At 73.9 to 74.1 s the red circle settles at diameters 124, 128, 132, 132, 133, 134, 134 px, with no overshoot. At 157.4 to 157.77 s the final circle grows about 2x in roughly 11 frames. Of the 91 large motion bursts, 65% reach peak frame-to-frame change within their first 3 frames, which is a fast-attack, long-settle profile.

At 72.67 s a white ball falls from the top onto a stack, on 'que tu utiliseras'. Top-edge y per frame: 175, 211, 240, 264, 281, 294, 304, 309, 313, 314, 314. The remaining distance shrinks by a ratio of about 0.74, 0.72, 0.68, 0.66, 0.60, which fits a cubic ease-out. The ball does not bounce or squash on landing.

entrances.type: morph / re-arrangement of the existing set into the next composition
entrances.easing: ease-out (fast start); individual parts sometimes staggered by 1 to 3 frames
entrances.notes: This is the main way visuals enter. Examples: 33 circles in a 3x12 grid become 7 circles in a row at 1.27 to 1.6 s ('33 ans' then '7 choses'), and change to 20 circles and back at 2.6 and 3.27 s. A line with circles becomes a trapezoid and then a triangle at 30.37 to 30.8 s. Scattered shapes collapse into a pyramid stack at 72.0 to 72.3 s. A stack becomes a row of circles with an enlarged red circle at 73.63 to 74.03 s. Outgoing parts shrink toward their own centres or to dots while incoming parts grow, all at the same time.
At 120.77 s a black square enters from the left as a thin vertical bar and widens to full size in about 6 frames, while the 3x3 grid it replaces shrinks away.

entrances.type: reposition (slide) of an element already on screen
entrances.notes: At 123.05 to 123.6 s the red circle slides right from x 275 to 403. Per-frame speed (px per 3 frames) is 7, 20, 36, 38, 18, 7.5, 0.4, a symmetric slow-in and slow-out. This is the only ease-in-out profile found: moves use ease-in-out, while appearances and changes in scale or rotation use ease-out.
At 121.57 s a square tilts about 15 to 20 degrees on 'c'est choisir', then holds. Frame-to-frame change decays from 2.8 to 0.1 over 14 frames.

Used only for typographic or UI content. '€ / MOIS' fades in at about 51.5 s, then a red '5' fades in on the word '5 euros' at 52.3 s. On the end card the heart outline and the 'S'ABONNER' button fade in at 158.13 to 158.33 s.

From 46.6 to 50.9 s a white message card is typed one character at a time in sync with the voice. 'À : Moi, 20 ans' is typed while 'à mon moi de 20 ans' is spoken, then 'Commence à investir.' and 'Renseigne-toi.', each with a blinking text cursor. Before the card resizes into the next composition, its content fades out over about 0.2 s.
At 157.8 to 158.1 s the big red circle changes into a squircle and then a rounded card while its fill crossfades red to salmon to pale pink to white (about 10 frames).

idle_motion: The brief assumed continuous animation; the measurements contradict it. 52% of content frames are pixel-identical to the previous frame (mean absolute difference below 0.02/255 over the visual band). For example, 70.0 to 71.8 s has 54 identical frames in a row, and still holds last up to about 2.2 s (65 frames at 66.9 s, 63 frames at 26.1 s, 62.7 s and 97.9 s). Nothing breathes, floats, wobbles or parallaxes. There is no camera move or zoom: the grid lines sit at the same pixel positions (x = 19, 38, 58...) in every sampled frame, and the background has no grain (frame-to-frame difference 0.0). The video feels alive for three other reasons. (1) A visual event starts about once per second (median 1.03 s between onsets), each on a spoken word. (2) The karaoke accent jumps every 0.13 to 0.2 s and the caption group changes every 0.6 s. (3) A few slow linear narrative drifts run while the voice continues. Example: on 'ne veut pas pour autant dire que ce sera une tâche facile', the red ball rolls steadily up the triangle's slope from 30.8 to 32.7 s at a constant 11 px per 0.2 s (about 55 px/s at 576, about 103 px/s at 1080). The speed is perfectly linear and holds for about 2 s, so the motion illustrates effort. Between events, every element holds its exact final pose.
transitions_between_visuals: There are no hard cuts in the content. The only single-frame visual jump in 161 s is the subscribe button popping back at 159.67 s. Every handover is a choreographed morph lasting 0.3 to 0.45 s (1.27 to 1.6 s: 0.33 s; 30.37 to 30.8 s: 0.43 s; 73.63 to 74.03 s: 0.40 s; 120.77 to 121.0 s: about 0.33 s with a 0.1 s tail). Outgoing elements shrink toward their own centres, or to small dots or squares that then vanish, while incoming elements grow or slide in. Both happen in the same frames. Elements that carry meaning persist and move to their new place instead of disappearing; the red 'protagonist' circle survives most handovers. The stage is never empty: the visual band only nears empty during the deliberate 'dans le présent' scatter of tiny dots at 65.3 to 66.0 s. Frame-to-frame change peaks in the first 1 to 3 frames of the handover and then decays, an ease-out profile, for example 21.9, 22.0, 16.3, 13.3, 8.7, 5.6, 3.2, 1.6, 0.6, 0.1 at 120.77 s. A handover starts on a word onset and usually on a caption group change: 57% of major-change starts fall within 2 frames of a group start, and 89% within 2 frames of a word onset. A recurring 'chapter' composition marks list items. On 'Numéro 2', 'Numéro 4' and 'Numéro 5', the scene morphs into a row of 7 small white outlined circles with the Nth one enlarged and red, used as a progress indicator, for about 1 to 1.3 s. It then morphs into the item's illustration.
sync_rules: The reference syncs everything to word onsets, frame-accurately, with no lead or lag. (1) Karaoke against audio: I cross-correlated the 795 word-highlight switch times with a speech-band onset function (300 to 4000 Hz, 10 ms hop). The peak is at +10 ms (score 4.6, against about 3.3 for lags beyond ±100 ms), so the highlight switches in the same frame as the word's acoustic onset. (2) Motion against words: of 107 motion onsets that follow a still hold, 83 start in exactly the same frame as a karaoke word switch, and 92% within ±2 frames. A random-time baseline gives 57% at ±2 frames. Only 44 of the 107 coincide with a caption group start, so events are tied to keywords, often in the middle of a group, not only to group changes. (3) Captions against pauses: the voice is edited tight. There are 83 pauses of 80 ms or more (speech band 11 dB below median): median 0.12 s, p90 0.20 s, max 0.31 s. 70 of the 83 pauses contain a caption group change. The new group appears 0 to 50 ms before speech resumes (56 of about 94 cases fall in that bin), so the old caption stays through the pause and the new one appears with its first word. The other roughly 200 group changes happen mid-phrase, purely by word count. A caption is always visible after 0.07 s; there are no blank frames between groups. (4) Semantic sync: visuals change on the word that names them. 33 circles appear on '33 ans', 7 on '7 choses', 20 on '20 ans', the red '5' on '5 euros', the ball drops on 'utiliseras', and the typed text follows the spoken text. Implementation rule: trigger = round(word.start × 30), from word-level timestamps.

captions.words_per_group_typical: 2 to 4, mode 3 (272 groups: 1 word ×5, 2 words ×71, 3 words ×136, 4 words ×60; mean 2.92). Each group lasts a median of 0.60 s (p10 0.30, p90 0.93, max 2.03 s).
captions.font_weight: Inter Bold (700), possibly with tracking near -0.5%. Fitted on the 'pour autant dire' width of 265 px at 576: Inter Bold 34 px gives 264 px; on 'J'ai 33 ans' the measurement is 182 px and Bold 34 gives 180 px. The 'd' ascender is 26 px tall. 34 px at 576 is 64 px at 1080.
captions.text_color: Warm near-black ink, about #1A1611 (measured 26,22,17), on cream about #F3EDDF; contrast 15.4:1. No stroke, no shadow, no background box. Natural sentence case ('J'ai', 'Mais', 'Numéro', 'Et' are capitalised; everything else is lowercase). Punctuation is stripped except apostrophes and hyphens. Numbers are written as digits ('33', '7', '20', '5 euros').
captions.highlight_color: Vermilion, about #E5542F (fill measured 232,84,48; antialiased text 224,85,53), the same colour as the red protagonist shapes. Contrast against the cream background is only 3.1:1.
captions.highlight_rule: Karaoke. Exactly one word per group is accented at any time: the word being spoken. The accent starts on the first word when the group appears and steps word by word. It is not a fixed keyword per group.
captions.highlight_evidence: (a) Consecutive frames inside one group, at 15 and 30 fps. 'J'ai 33 ans': 'J'ai' is red at 0.07 s, '33' at 0.20 to 0.40 s, 'ans' at 0.47 to 0.87 s. 'et voici 7 choses': 'et' at 0.93 s, 'voici' at 1.0 to 1.2 s, '7' at 1.27 to 1.4 s, 'choses' at 1.47 to 1.6 s. 'pour autant dire': 'pour' at 30.87 s, 'autant' at 31.0 to 31.2 s, 'dire' from 31.27 s. 'on veut réagir': 'on' at 122.07 s, 'veut' at 122.2 s, 'réagir' at 122.27 to 122.87 s. (b) Full-video scan at 30 fps of the caption band: every caption frame from 0.07 to 161.2 s contains red pixels. There are 523 in-group accent jumps (the red mask moves while the text mask is unchanged), which is (words per group - 1) per group. (c) The jump times line up with the acoustic word onsets (cross-correlation peak at +10 ms). (d) The colour switch is instant: no intermediate brown pixels at the switch frame (0.2 px on average against 0.3 baseline), and in only 1 of 200 switches do two words look red at once.
captions.caption_transitions: Hard cut, both between groups and between accented words. The text mask changes completely in one frame; the only multi-frame case (80.7 s) is a shape passing over the caption. Text width at frames 0, 1 and 3 of a group is identical (126.1, 126.1, 126.1 px at 288 wide), so there is no scale pop, fade or slide-in. Text width varies by at most 1 px within a group, so nothing moves. The caption is centred horizontally (centre x 287 to 288 of 576). The baseline is fixed at y = 720/1024 (70.3%, so y = 1350 at 1920). Ascender top is at 694/1024 (y = 1301) and descender bottom at 726 (y = 1361); the text block centre is about 69.0%. Width: median 44% of the frame width (about 475 px at 1080), p90 61% (about 660 px). A caption is always one line; no second line was ever detected.

background: Flat cream graph paper, completely static. Fill about #F3EDDF (measured 242 to 243, 236 to 237, 222 to 223). Grid lines about #E9E3D4 (233,227,212), only 4% darker than the fill. Lines are 1 px at 576 (about 2 px at 1080), spaced 19.2 px (19 or 20 px alternating), which makes exactly 30 columns across, or 36 px spacing at 1080. The grid is uniform with no darker major lines. The first line sits at x = 19 and y = 19, so the grid is anchored to the frame's top-left corner. The grid never moves (line positions are identical at 0, 30, 70 and 121 s). No vignette (corner luminance 241.4, centre 241.6, bottom 241.9), no grain or noise (frame-to-frame difference 0.0, spatial standard deviation 0.07), and no gradient. Shapes are opaque and hide the grid. The neo-brutalist shape style is part of the background contrast: flat fills (vermilion, ink black, white, a pale pink accent around #F5C9BE and salmon around #EC8A72), a 3 px stroke in ink black at 576 (about 5 to 6 px at 1080), and a hard ink-black drop shadow offset about +4/+4 px at 576 (about 7 to 8 px at 1080) with no blur.
end_card: The creator's own outro runs from 156.0 to 161.2 s. The black TikTok logo screen from 161.2 to 165.2 s is TikTok's download watermark, not part of the design, and should not be copied. Sequence: 'Le seul moment que tu vis réellement' shows a timeline (past dot, line, a red 'present' circle, a dashed future circle). On 'c'est maintenant' (157.4 to 157.77 s) the red circle grows about 2x with an ease-out to fill about 40% of the width while the line retracts. On 'En attendant' (157.8 to 158.1 s) the circle becomes a squircle and then a white rounded card, its fill crossfading red to salmon to pink to white in about 0.3 s. At 158.13 to 158.33 s a heart outline icon in the card and a red 'S'ABONNER' pill button below it (white ExtraBold uppercase, hard shadow) fade in over 0.2 s. At 158.43 to 158.57 s an arrow cursor enters from the lower right and glides to the heart. On 'like la vidéo' (158.63 to 158.77 s) a click fills the heart red over about 0.15 s, with a 3-tick burst at the click point. Before 'abonne-toi' (159.27 to 159.43 s) the cursor moves down to the button. At 159.53 to 159.67 s the button is pressed: it shifts down-right into its own shadow for about 3 frames, then pops back. The card then holds completely still, with the caption 'et abonne-toi', until 161.2 s. The voice ends at 160.07 s (silencedetect), so the card holds silently for about 1.1 s after the last word.
other_details: Format and audio: 576x1024 at 30 fps, real 30 fps animation (no duplicated frames during motion). The audio's integrated loudness is -14.1 LUFS with a 0 dBFS peak. The voice is the focus. Inter-word pauses sit around -37.5 dBFS (median), 21 dB under the voice (about -16 dBFS RMS), and contain no consistent tonal content. A music bed, if present, is at least 20 dB down; voice alone is a faithful choice.

Visuals are literal: each shape set illustrates the keyword being spoken. Counts match spoken numbers (33, 7 and 20 circles). Metaphors are acted out: a ball pushed uphill means 'not easy', scattered pieces collapse into a stack for 'tirer des leçons', a seesaw means 'injuste', a 3x3 grid fills with dots for 'on ne choisit pas ses parents'. The visual vocabulary stays small and consistent: circles, squares and triangles, a single accent colour, and a recurring red protagonist circle.

Typographic cards: a white box with a hard shadow holds big numbers ('20 € / MOIS', with '20' or '5' in red ExtraBold at about 2x caption size) or a chat or e-mail card ('À : Moi, 20 ans' plus typed text). The red number appears exactly on its spoken word.
Chapter marker: on 'Numéro N', a row of 7 outlined circles with the Nth enlarged (about 1.6x) and filled red. It shows progress through the list and is reused for every item.

Colour discipline: one accent colour, shared by the caption's current word and the main element in the visual, which ties text and image together. Secondary tints of the same hue (salmon, pale pink) are used for bars and for the card crossfade.

Rhythm: all three layers run at different but phase-locked rates on the same clock (word onsets). The accent moves every word (about 0.13 to 0.2 s), the caption every 0.6 s, a visual event about every 1 s, a new composition every 1.3 to 2 s. Between beats everything holds perfectly still, which gives a crisp, edited, 'designed' feel instead of a floaty one.
Shapes may overlap the caption band in passing (circle at 80.7 s, drawn above the text), but compositions rest above it, leaving about 160 px of clear space.
A TikTok watermark (logo and '@ledevultime') appears top-left for the first second and bottom-right afterwards. It comes from TikTok's download and is not design.

Evidence files: scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cognitive-finance-systems/bcfb8b4b-777a-5deb-992e-068d24e12cb7/scratchpad/tools/ (sheet.py, cap_an.py, vis_an.py, sync_an.py, aud_an.py). Data and contact sheets are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cognitive-finance-systems/bcfb8b4b-777a-5deb-992e-068d24e12cb7/scratchpad/motion/. That folder holds the dense 15 fps windows sheet_w0_a/b.png, sheet_w30_a/b.png, sheet_w70_a/b.png and sheet_w120_a/b.png; the 30 fps sheets sheet_d72.png, sheet_d120.png and sheet_d158.png (end card); sheet_w46.png (typewriter and number card); sheet_end.png; and the measurement outputs cap_events.json, vis_events.json, pauses.json and illus_sheet.png (our illustrations on black).

V01 numbers for planning: 147 words over 0 to 57.54 s, 2.55 words/s, half the reference rate. 33 word gaps exceed 0.15 s (p90 gap 0.34 s). Segment boundaries: accroche 0 to 2.88, contexte 3.27 to 7.81, point1 8.31 to 23.2, point2 23.52 to 37.41, point3 37.92 to 50.46, chute 51.04 to 54.93, cta 55.27 to 57.54 s. Words in words.json carry punctuation ('heures', '?', 'étape :', 'fausse.') that has to be stripped for display.
recommendations_for_glass_version: Clock: drive every event from build/V01/words.json, using frame = round(start × 30). Add no lead or lag; the reference is frame-synchronous with word onsets (measured offset +10 ms). Check once that the ElevenLabs timestamps line up with audio.wav before relying on them.

Captions: Inter Bold 64 px, one line, centred at x = 540. Baseline at y = 1350 (text block about y 1301 to 1361, so about 69% of the height), well above TikTok's bottom 380 px. Use 2 to 3 words per group, 4 at most, and about 22 characters or 660 px wide at most. Break groups at punctuation and at word gaps above 0.15 s, otherwise by count. Show a group at its first word's onset and keep it on screen through the following pause, so no blank caption appears between groups. Cut hard between groups: no fade, pop, slide, stroke, shadow or box. Strip punctuation except apostrophes and hyphens, keep sentence case, and write numbers as digits ('9 h', '1 page', '10 min').

Caption colours on dark: base text in cream #F6F0E4 (17:1 on #0B0B0D). The accent is the currently spoken word (karaoke) with an instant colour switch. Brand red #C8102E reaches 3.3:1 on near-black, the same ratio as the reference's accent on cream (3.1:1). For better legibility after TikTok compression, use a brighter brand red such as #F0334A (4.9:1). Keep bordeaux #7A0E14 off text (1.8:1); use it only for fills or shadows.

Background: near-black #0B0B0D or similar, since the PNG halos were rendered for black and a lighter background makes them look washed out. Add the reference's graph paper inverted: a static 36 px grid (30 columns at 1080) anchored at the top-left, 2 px lines only 3 to 4% brighter than the fill (for example #16161A), with no major lines. The grid never moves and has no grain. The reference has no vignette. One optional extra: a very faint radial lift behind the hero at y about 800, so the glass reads, kept within about 5% luminance.

Hero placement: centre the object's opaque bounding box, not the 1536x1024 canvas, at x about 530 and y about 800 (42% of the height). Scale per image so the object box is at most about 780 px wide and 560 px tall. Object boxes range from 51% to 95% of canvas width (WTH-003-04 is narrow, WTH-003-08 wide), so normalise per image. This keeps the visual in roughly y 490 to 1140, out of the right 140 px and above the caption, with about 160 px of clear space.

Entrances for a glass hero: scale 0.7 to 1.0 with opacity 0 to 1, over 330 ms with a cubic ease-out (opacity complete by about 40% of the duration), no overshoot or elastic, starting on the keyword's frame. Small vector accents (dots, rings, step markers, number chips) pop from scale 0 to 1 in 300 ms with a cubic ease-out. Objects tied to 'arrive' or 'landing' words can drop from about 300 px above in 370 ms with a cubic ease-out and no bounce. Moving a hero that is already on screen, for example sliding it to x about 360 to make room for a chip: cubic ease-in-out over 500 to 550 ms. Rotation: ease-out over 450 ms.

Handover between heroes: never hard-cut. Start the outgoing and incoming animations in the same frame (a word onset, ideally a caption group start). The outgoing hero goes from scale 1.0 to 0.8 and opacity 1 to 0 in about 250 ms, ease-out, toward the incoming hero's centre to imitate a morph. The incoming hero grows from 0.7 to 1.0 in 330 to 400 ms. The stage is never empty. If something persists from one scene to the next (a red marker, a chip), move it to its new position instead of replacing it, as the reference does with its red circle.

Cadence for V01, compensating for the slower speech: one beat event about every 1.0 s on a keyword (about 50 to 55 events in 57.7 s), and a new hero every 2.5 to 3.5 s (about 16 to 20 heroes). The hook (0 to 3 s) should be denser, with a change about every 1 to 1.5 s. Use the 9 WTH-003 images first, plus relevant generic ones (AI, CRYSTAL, TARGET, TOKEN, GEAR, BOOK, FINGERPRINT, TAG…). Re-list assets/illustrations before finalising, and ignore WTH-002-*. Beats between hero swaps can be: a number chip popping in, a step marker, a red underline or dot appearing under part of the object, a slide of the hero to one side, or a short specular glint sweep (about 400 ms) across the glass on the keyword.

Idle motion: the reference is fully static between beats (52% of frames frozen), which reads as crisp, so keep heroes still apart from one subtle addition. The user rejected a static carousel, and raster objects lack the reference's vector motion, so give each hero a very slow linear push-in (scale +3 to 4% over its lifetime). Do not use floating, bobbing or random wobble. For metaphors the voice keeps describing, add one linear narrative drift at constant speed (about 100 px/s at 1080), like the reference's ball rolling uphill.

Semantic literalness: change or add the visual on the word that names it. Examples: clock WTH-003-01 plus a '9 h' chip on 'Client à 9 heures'; document WTH-003-04 on 'brief structuré d'une page'; the AI head on 'L'IA'; the vault WTH-003-03 on 'dossier client' and 'aucune donnée'; '10 min' on 'Dix minutes de relecture'. Number chips copy the reference's '20 € / MOIS' card adapted to dark: a dark rounded card (#141418) with a 2 px cream outline, cream ExtraBold units, and the digit in red at about 2x caption size. The digit fades or pops in on the spoken number.

Step marker, copying 'Numéro N': on 'Première étape', 'Ensuite' and 'Dernière étape', show a row of 3 cream outlined circles with the active one 1.6x larger and filled brand red. Hold for about 1.0 to 1.3 s, then morph into the step's hero. This also brings the caption accent colour into the visuals, as the reference's red protagonist does.

Hard shadows: the reference's flat style (3 px ink stroke plus a hard +4/+4 px offset shadow at 576) cannot be applied to photoreal glass and would be invisible on black anyway. Keep the glass clean, at most with a soft contact shadow or reflection ellipse underneath. On flat vector chips and markers, a hard 6 to 8 px offset in bordeaux #7A0E14 echoes the reference's neo-brutalist signature.

End card (cta, 55.27 to 57.54 s): the last hero shrinks and morphs into a dark rounded card in about 0.3 s. At the 'Abonne-toi' onset, a heart outline and a brand-red 'S'ABONNER' pill fade in over 0.2 s. Optionally, a cursor glides in (0.2 s) and clicks: the heart fills red over 0.15 s with a 3-tick burst, and the button press dips into its offset shadow for 3 frames. Hold the final frame still for about 1.2 to 1.5 s after the last word, so the video ends around 58.8 to 59.0 s, inside 60 s. Add no platform-style outro.
Audio: keep the voice-only mix at -14 LUFS, matching the reference's -14.1 LUFS. If a music bed is added later, keep it at least 20 dB under the voice.
